newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thai premier contemplates political doom at summit.
newsitem.headline: Thai premier contemplates political doom at summit.

text.p: Amid the beams and bonhomie of the APEC summit, one leader looked at times like a man preparing for his own execution.
And in a sense he was. Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa of Thailand probably would be out of office before the day ended.

Thai voters killed off his scandal-tainted premiership in a general election a week ago, and his successor was expected to be appointed on Monday night, possibly even before the summit ended in the Philippines.

In sharp contrast to the visage Banharn presented as leaders of half the world's people gathered for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, back home the Thai stock market was bubbling merrily in anticipation of his political demise.
Investors were confident an economic advisory team under new Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh would be able to tackle Thailand's economic ills.

The rush was on in Bangkok to cut through political red tape and have Prime Minister-designate Chavalit speedily installed in time to welcome U.S. President Bill Clinton from Manila for his state visit to Thailand late on Monday.
Clinton thus would be able to say goodbye to one Thai prime minister and hello to another within 24 hours.
Banharn on Monday gave Philippine President Fidel Ramos a watery smile when he arrived at the summit.
But every now and then the diminutive 64-year-old -- at 160 cm (five feet three inches) he's the shortest APEC leader -- looked quite downcast despite the picture-perfect sunny day in Subic Bay.
As his counterparts loosened the necks of their casual Barong shirts to conform with Philippine custom, Banharn stayed tightly buttoned-up.
Perhaps he was contemplating the highs and lows of life in a the democratic political jungle as he stood beneath the gently rustling palm fronds on the edge of a cliff by Subic Bay.
There close by was Clinton, his power and influence rejuvenated by a sweeping election victory 20 days ago.
Only eight months ago Banharn himself was at the peak, hosting a landmark summit of 25 European and Asian leaders with bands and banners in his own capital.
It has been all downhill since.
